title: Silent quarantine of healthy nodes triggered multi-tier fallback storm
creator: Leah Turner
description: During a routine rollout of an optimization that filters noisy heartbeat signals at the routing controller, a logical issue caused a subset of healthy worker nodes to be classified as quarantined. The controller suppressed these nodes from eligible candidate pools without emitting explicit drain events. The silent quarantine progressively reduced available capacity in primary tiers and regions, which caused automatic routing policies to shift traffic to fallback model variants and lower tiers across multiple regions. The fallback amplification led to capacity saturation, increased latency, and higher per-token costs for impacted customer traffic. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and follow-ups.
incident_summary: A heartbeat-filtering rule erroneously quarantined healthy hosts without drain signals, triggering broad fallback routing across tiers and regions and producing a spike in latency and failed SLOs; immediate rollback and traffic caps restored stability.
timeline: 2026-03-10T02:04Z - New heartbeat filter rollout (PR #4218) completed on routing-controlplane-canary
2026-03-10T02:20Z - First SLO alert: increased 99th pct latency for hosted-api-us-west

2026-03-10T02:30Z - On-call paged; initial hypothesis: slow decommissioning or regional networking issue
2026-03-10T02:42Z - Investigation discovered controller excluded ~38% of healthy nodes via quorum check in heartbeat filter; nodes appeared offline to the routing decision path
2026-03-10T02:50Z - Temporary mitigation: rollback heartbeat filter flag and apply conservative weight caps on fallback variants (hybrid routing policy), traffic rebalanced
2026-03-10T03:15Z - Latency and error rates return to baseline; post-incident monitoring enabled on routing eligibility signals

root_cause: The new heartbeat filtering logic used an optimistic edge-case path that dropped hosts that had intermittent zero-latency probes (numeric underflow in aggregation window). Because the code path updated the in-memory eligible set without emitting drains or tombstones, the scheduler and routing policies treated those hosts as permanently unavailable. Automatic fallback policies then reweighted traffic to alternative variants and lower tiers, amplifying downstream capacity pressure and causing a cascading fallback storm.
detection: Detected by SLO alerts (99p latency) and corroborated by capacity heatmaps showing sudden capacity loss with no drain events. Correlation of routing eligibility snapshots with deployment timeline pointed to the recent heartbeat-filter rollout (PR #4218). Pager duty rotation and the routing-controlplane logs provided the traces showing suppressed eligibility updates.
immediate_mitigation: Rollback heartbeat filter flag to previous stable config (rolled back at 2026-03-10T02:50Z)
Inject conservative caps on fallback variant weights to prevent over-concentration of traffic (runtime flag applied)
Temporary routing circuit-breaker: stop promoting fallback variants above 30% of regional traffic until eligibility signal validation passes
Enable high-fidelity logging for routing eligibility changes and emit explicit drain events when hosts are removed from eligible sets
long_term_fix: Replace optimistic heartbeat path with robust aggregation that handles zero/NaN probe outcomes and validates numeric stability
Ensure any change to eligible node sets emits an auditable drain/tombstone event that downstream systems can observe
Add unit and integration tests that simulate intermittent probe values and validate that sane eligibility sets are maintained
Introduce a canary stage for routing eligibility logic with traffic shadowing and traffic caps before global rollout
Enhance fallback policy throttles: dynamic backoff based on real-time queue depth and token-cost signals
Add a cross-region routing simulation harness to exercise multi-tier fallback behavior under partial-capacity loss

notes: This incident surfaced a blind spot: routing eligibility changes that are not surfaced as explicit control-plane events can produce silent capacity loss; we must treat eligibility updates as first-class events.
Consider adding a periodic reconciler that compares the control-plane eligible set with agent heartbeats and emits corrective actions if divergence is detected.
Technical debt: evaluate the number handling across routing/control plane to avoid NaN/underflow in aggregations
